author: T. R. Shockley
title: OCBC expands physical gold offering for institutional and private banking clients
text:
OCBC expands physical gold offering for institutional and private banking clients
OCBC announced on June 8 that it will expand its gold proposition to include physical gold transactions for institutional clients and Bank of Singapore's high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients, starting June 10. Clients will be able to buy, sell, and store large gold bars and kilobars in a secure vault located in Singapore.
The bank said this move is part of a strategy to strengthen OCBC’s capabilities in precious metals amid rising global demand for gold bars. According to the World Gold Council, demand for gold bars in the first quarter of 2026 increased by 50% compared to the previous year. The bank reported that Bank of Singapore client holdings for physical gold have grown more than 40% since the end of 2025, with most holdings attributed to ultra-high-net-worth individuals.
Previously, Bank of Singapore clients transacted physical gold through a US-based entity. Now, they can do so with OCBC in Singapore. The bank said that clients are increasingly seeking local bullion storage and prefer dealing with Singapore-based entities due to geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty.
OCBC will offer two sizes: large bars (about 400 troy ounces or 12.4 kg), which are standard for international trade settlement, and kilobars (1 kg), which are common in Asian markets and accepted by Commodity Exchange futures contracts in the United States. Each bar is serial-numbered and allocated specifically to individual clients rather than pooled reserves.
Jason Moo, CEO of Bank of Singapore, said, “Gold has long played a strategic role in wealth preservation, particularly for ultra-high-net-worth clients with long-term, intergenerational objectives. Amid market volatility and geopolitical uncertainty, these clients are thinking more deeply about who they transact with, and where their gold is stored. By leveraging OCBC Group’s strengths, we will be able to deliver a secure, trusted and differentiated physical gold offering that addresses our clients’ risk concerns.”
Kenneth Lai, Head of Global Markets at OCBC, added: “Our Singapore-based physical gold trading and custodian capabilities represent a strategic expansion of our market-making capabilities in precious metals. While we have started with private banking, over time we are looking to expand to institutional as well as other client segments, and offer them a comprehensive range of physical gold investment and hedging solutions.”
